title: VideoAnalysisRequest
description: The request that triggers analyze-content-video. It covers the three product-spec entry points as one envelope and declares capability needs, not providers: the Skill selects a workflow and the Connector Runtime resolves which connector and operation serves it. Acquisition parameters here map one-to-one onto real connector parameters; nothing describes an algorithm no registered connector implements.

source.description: Two orthogonal questions. `acquisition` says how the media is obtained and drives which connector operations apply. `subject_state` says whose content it is and at what stage, and drives what the analysis may conclude. They do not imply each other: an uploaded file may be the creator's own draft or somebody else's video the creator downloaded to study.

acquisition.description: Where the media comes from, and therefore who reads it. local_file is read on this machine by this package's own scripts; public_url and owner_connector are read by connectors. The two paths never serve one request: they would be reading two different copies of the video.

subject_state.description: Whose content this is and whether it is published. It cannot be inferred from the media or from the acquisition path: the same file may be the creator's unreleased draft or a competitor's post. For a public URL without an ownership statement, explicitly declare unknown and use public-only evidence; never infer own or third_party. Unknown permits neither owner data nor a baseline.

platform.description: For an unpublished draft this is the intended platform; use `unknown` only when the creator genuinely has not decided.

file_ref.description: Absolute path to the media on the machine this Skill runs on. No connector reads it: the media capability runs server-side and cannot see this file under any name, so a local_file request is served by this package's own local scripts and must never spend a media-connector call on it. There is no workspace root. An earlier version of this description said the media connector accepted files under one, which was never true, and a real run spent six calls discovering that - every one rejected at request validation, none creating a job - before it could attempt anything else.

owner_data.description: Where owner metrics come from. Meaningful only when subject_state is own_published; owner metrics never exist for third-party content and do not exist yet for an unpublished draft.

allOf.$comment: required alone only checks that a key is present, so each branch also pins the type: a null file_ref is not a file reference.

acquire.description: Capability needs and how strictly each is required. 'required' makes a failure fatal, 'best_effort' records the failure state and continues, 'skip' spends nothing on it.

transcript_language.description: Caption fetching is language-scoped and defaults to English. A language with no captions returns an empty transcript and a partial status rather than an error, so the caller should state it.

frame_timestamps.description: Explicit sampling seconds. Required for any hook-window or first-frame dimension, because the default evenly spaced selection places its first frame at duration/(n+1) and cannot reach the opening seconds. Mutually exclusive with frame_count.

frame_count.description: Evenly spaced sampling count. Mutually exclusive with frame_timestamps.

baseline.description: Optional account context. Without it the deterministic verdicts can only be 'unassessed'; the analysis still runs.

budget.description: Workflow-level ceiling. The Connector Runtime budgets a single call at a time, so per-call limits are passed straight through while the call count and any metered credits are governed here. This block is mandatory because a reviewed candidate was observed selecting accounts on its own and starting paid scraping seconds after receiving a token, with no confirmation step anywhere in its workflow.

max_connector_calls.description: Zero permits analysis of existing evidence only; every acquire capability must be skip.

confirmed_by_user.description: Must be true before any billable call. A request may be built with false and held until the creator approves.

per_call.description: Passed verbatim into each connector request budget.

on_missing_capability.description: Whichever is chosen, a partial result must never be presented as complete.

fatal_capabilities.description: Capabilities whose absence aborts the request regardless of the policy above. Anything listed here should also be 'required' in acquire.
